regional_assessment: East Asian monsoon zone exhibits strong thermal-rainfall gradients; maize yields (median 5.20 t/ha) correlate with thermal accumulation (tmin median 9.64°C) and radiation stress (cwb median -2.06), necessitating conservative development thresholds to capture 90th percentile growing conditions while excluding frost-risk and drought-stress extremes.

candidates.agronomic_rationale: Captures primary yield driver (GDD) using median tmin (9.64°C) as base to reflect typical monsoon onset, with upper limit (34.62°C) capping at tmax 90th percentile to exclude heat-shock outliers; stress thresholds target the 5th-10th percentiles of tmin/tmax/prec to filter non-viable growing windows.

Prioritizes radiation (rad) and cloudless clearness index (cwb) as proxies for photosynthetic potential, setting GDD base to tmin 25th percentile (7.12°C) to ensure sufficient cold accumulation, while upper limit (33.00°C) prevents extreme tmax (>35°C) days that degrade radiation efficiency; precipitation threshold (0.37mm) filters dry spells during critical vegetative stages.

Targets high-yield outliers by relaxing GDD base to tmin 10th percentile (0.94°C) to include warmer northern zones, raising upper limit to tmax 95th percentile (31.25°C) to capture heat-stressed but potentially high-radiation scenarios, and tightening precipitation threshold (1.0mm) to identify early drought onset risks that suppress yield despite high thermal sums.
